target: For every closed oriented genus g>=2 and every finite symmetric mapping-class-group generating set S, the Torelli fraction in distinct-element ambient word balls tends to zero.
accepted_conclusions: Exponential Torelli negligibility after a suitable finite symmetric generating-set enlargement containing any prescribed finite subset, with explicit spectral/free-subgroup constants.
Complete authored F_3 x F_2 counterexample to general transfer across generating sets: density 1/3 for the sum metric and zero for the max metric.
Logarithmic liminf at least 1/2 for every finite symmetric generating set of the closed genus-g mapping class group, g>=2.
Both generating-set infima, for logarithmic liminf and limsup, equal 1/2 even when the generating sets must contain a fixed finite subset.
remaining_gap: Ordinary density zero in every previously fixed arbitrary finite symmetric word metric; existence or an exact value of the logarithmic limit for a fixed generating set is not established.
mathematical_dependencies: The elementary enlargement argument is proved in full. The logarithmic appendix uses attributed Torelli pseudo-Anosov existence, McCarthy virtually cyclic centralizers and the standard positive Teichmuller-axis translation fact. McCarthy source verification is text-only and is not a new audit of its proof.
